title: Canonical derived localization and scalar squares on signed point lines
statement: For a finite-field datum and prime different from its characteristic, the point Tate carriers and fixed composites [def-pur-point-tate-comparison-data] and the constructed canonical comparisons [def-pur-point-tate-canonical-comparisons] obey three exact coordinate equations, on the signed integral and rational Tate lines [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], with the prime made invertible on the point as in [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], and with the rational point fibre, its coefficient descent, carrier lift and tensor/lift comparisons of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and the derived field scalar extension of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. RationalLineNormalization is rationalSizeNormalization followed by coefficient descent of rawRationalSingle, then the descent/single comparison and single of the fixed rational coefficient tensor transport. Single of canonicalIntegral is completedSectionsComparison with canonicalSheaf. The carrier lift of rationalPointComparison with canonicalSheaf, followed by rationalLineNormalization, is the recorded tensor/lift isomorphism followed by scalar extension of the source normalization, the field tensor/single comparison, and single of canonicalRational. These are equations of the specified maps, with no generator or free comparison witness quantified.

proof.text: expand rationalLineNormalization and pointRationalNormalization. Their initial composites are precisely rationalSizeNormalization. On a degree-zero integral line the remaining pointFibreRationalDownIso is the derived natural isomorphism of the normalized coefficient tensor transport. Compatibility of mapDerivedCategoryNatIso with single objects, and the composition formula for mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor, identify it with down.map(rawRationalSingle), the down/single comparison, and single.map of the tensor transport, in that order. For the completed square expand completedSectionsComparison and completedLineComparison. Substitute the definition of pointSectionsScalarExtensionIso: its inverse is the derived sections-tensor map followed by sections of the completion comparison. The latter cancels its inverse in completedLineComparison. Naturality of the exact-single comparisons moves the ordinary line isomorphism through sections. The result is single.map of pointSectionsTensor followed by sections of canonicalSheaf, which is single.map canonicalIntegral. For the rational point square apply the defining normalized equation of pointRationalFibreScalar_existsUnique on the integral signed line. Naturality of the size-descent comparisons moves the fibre of integralLineComparison through pointIntegralRationalNormalization. Insert the rational scalar extension object equality occurring in rationalLineComparison; transport cancels with the same object equality in the defining scalar comparison. Rationalize the completed square just proved. The localization-tensor associator is the specified pointTensorRationalization, so its inverse followed by rationalization of canonicalIntegral is exactly canonicalRational. Finally cancel the inverse scalar comparison and insert the exact-single comparisons. This gives the displayed point equation, retaining the recorded lift/tensor and size-descent maps.

theorem canonicalDerivedCoordinates (hl : l ≠ D.p) :
    (∀ (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra (Padic l) F]
        [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) F] (m : ℤ),
      (rationalLineNormalization D l F hl m).hom =
        (rationalSizeNormalization D l F hl m).hom ≫
          (Functor.mapDerivedCategory.{u + 1, u + 2, u + 1, u + 1, u + 2, u + 2}
            (pointFibreCoefficientDown F)).map
            (rawRationalSingle D l F m).hom ≫
          ((pointFibreCoefficientDown F).mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app _ ≫
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).map
            ((pointFibreRationalDown_existsUnique D l F).exists.choose.hom.app
              (integralTwistLine l F (Spec (.of D.k)) m))) ∧
    (∀ (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra (Padic l) F]
        [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) F] (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra (Padic l) L]
        [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) L] (ι : F →ₐ[Padic l] L) (m : ℤ),
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).map
          (canonicalIntegral D l hl F L ι m).hom =
        completedSectionsComparison D l F hl L ι m (canonicalSheaf D l hl)) ∧
    (∀ (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra (Padic l) F]
        [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) F] (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra (Padic l) L]
        [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) L] (ι : F →ₐ[Padic l] L) (m : ℤ),
      letI := frobeniusPointPrimeInvertible D l hl
      (Functor.mapDerivedCategory.{u, u + 2, u, u + 1, u + 1, u + 2}
        (ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} L)).map
          (rationalPointComparison D l F hl L ι m (canonicalSheaf D l hl)).hom.hom ≫
        (rationalLineNormalization D l L hl m).hom =
      (pointFibreTensorLiftIso l F L ι).hom.app
          ((pointRationalFibre D l hl F).obj
            (sfRationalTwistingCoefficient l F (Spec (.of D.k)) m)).obj ≫
        (pointCoefficientFieldDerivedTensor l F L ι).map
          (rationalLineNormalization D l F hl m).hom ≫
        ((ModuleCat.extendScalars ι.toRingHom).mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app
          (rational D l F m) ≫
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).map (canonicalRational D l hl F L ι m).hom)
